title: Where does the energy go?
question: How does the mass of water affect its temperature rise when the same energy is transferred?

parameters.label: Specific heat capacity / J g⁻¹ K⁻¹

method: Hold energy and specific heat capacity constant. Record at least three different masses and repeat a reading to compare variation.
explanation: This model uses ΔT = q/(mc), assumes uniform temperature and no heat loss, and adds small simulated measurement variation. A real calorimeter also absorbs energy.
reflection: Use your readings to explain the relationship. Explain why a temperature rise is not itself an enthalpy change, and name one limitation of this model.

check.prompt: Fresh check: 100 g of water absorbs 4180 J. With c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ and no heat loss, find the temperature rise in K.

title: Same yield, different rate
question: Can a reaction reach the same final gas volume at different speeds?
method: Keep the rate constant and final volume fixed while taking readings at different times. Then clear the table and repeat with a larger rate constant. Export the first set before clearing if you want to keep both.
explanation: This illustrative model is V = Vfinal(1 − exp(−kt)). It describes an approach to a fixed yield; it is not a universal rate law and does not model every reaction or gas loss.
reflection: Describe how the slope changes during a run. Distinguish a change in rate from a change in final yield. Support your claim with readings.

check.prompt: Fresh check: gas volume increases from 12 to 30 cm³ over 15 s. Calculate the average rate in cm³ s⁻¹.
check.hint: Use change in volume divided by elapsed time.
